### How many humanoid robots exist in 2026?
Global humanoid robot shipments reached an estimated 16,000–18,000 units in 2025 — a 508% year-over-year increase — with Chinese manufacturers accounting for approximately 90% of volume.
Total active commercial deployments (productive work, not R&D) are estimated at fewer than 3,000–4,000 units globally, concentrated at Amazon, GXO, BMW, Hyundai, Mercedes-Benz, and Toyota facilities.
The gap between “shipped” and “productively deployed” is the most important number most analyses omit.

Twenty-nine target work or development; only one full-size model targets the home.

Twenty-nine were built for work or development.
Only four served the home, education or broader consumer market.
Just one was a full-size humanoid explicitly pitched for the home, and it was taking preorders rather than making immediate deliveries.
...
Only four qualifying families sat outside the work-and-development market: 1X NEO, Maxtronics NAO6, Noetix Dora and Robosen K1 Pro.
...
RoboZaps, which publishes the catalogue used in this analysis, froze the 74 rows returned by its live Humanoids filter on July 16, 2026.
The review counted one current bipedal family when first-party evidence showed a manufacturer-backed order, paid reservation or preorder, product-specific quote, lease or Robots-as-a-Service route, commercial delivery or committed external fleet.
Duplicate listings, configurations and predecessor generations were consolidated.
Thirty-three families qualified: 29 work or developer families and four home, education or consumer families.
Thirty-eight rows did not clear the test, while three remained unresolved.

content.text:
There’s no single definitive count—it depends on what “commercial” means. **About 14 models** are listed as commercially available for purchase or preorder in one 2026 industry tally; a broader catalog counts **44 models you can order**, including enterprise-only offerings.[1][2]

If you mean robots **already doing productive commercial work**, one estimate puts the total below **3,000–4,000 units worldwide**; many shipped robots are still used for research, demonstrations, or training.[3][6]
